ojluni-time.skipped: GenericArrayTypeImpl cannot be cast to java.lang.Class
ojluni-time.why: TestNG reads a data provider's generic return type, Iterator<Object[]>, and casts its type argument to Class. AOSP's libcore.reflect.GenericSignatureParser makes a GenericArrayTypeImpl for every array type argument and nothing resolves it to a Class (as on a device), so the Wasm tier, which runs that bytecode, skips these tests. The JS tier's reflection spec answers Object[].class.
These compare System.currentTimeMillis with Clock.systemUTC() readings taken moments apart; on a loaded host either tier fails them in some runs.

guava.why: The JS tier's ArrayDeque and ArrayBlockingQueue toArray(T[]) do not throw ArrayStoreException for an array of the wrong element type (JUnit: toArray(notAssignableTo[]) should throw); the Wasm tier runs the AOSP bytecode, which does.
